description: Disjoint splitting is a way for CBS to split a conflict so that the two subtrees share no solution. For a conflict between agents `a` and `b`, CBS picks one agent `i`. One child forbids the conflict to `i` with a *negative constraint*; the other child requires it of `i` with a *positive constraint* ("`i` must be at `v` at time `t`"), which forbids the conflict to every other agent. No plan lies below both children, so CBS does less duplicate work and stays optimal. `mapf-search` picks as `i` the agent whose MDD forces it through the conflict, if exactly one does, and uses the required vertices as landmarks in the low level; select it with `Splitting::Disjoint`.

papers.authors: Jiaoyang Li, Daniel Harabor, Peter J. Stuckey, Ariel Felner, Hang Ma, Sven Koenig
papers.title: Disjoint Splitting for Multi-Agent Path Finding with Conflict-Based Search
papers.venue: International Conference on Automated Planning and Scheduling (ICAPS)

lineage.source: mapf-search, src/cbs.rs: "Disjoint splitting (Li et al. 2019): one child forbids the conflict to one agent, the other requires it of that agent with a positive constraint"
